occurredAt.source: the clock that the event names

recordedAt.source: the wall clock of the host that ran the record command

doesNotEstablish: That a caller obtained or lost a completion at any instant. An event is a record of the control of the run or of an operator. It is not a request that a caller sent and had answered.
That a fault took effect, or when. An event states that a command was about to be issued and that it returned.
That a detection was correct. The event detection-reviewed states that an operator recorded a judgement.
That a reversal reached the cluster. The event reversal-accepted states that an acceptance was recorded, and a commit identifier is what the recorder stated.
That no other action was taken. A log holds each event that was recorded, and an action that nobody recorded is in no log.
A detection lag, a decision time, a recovery time, or any other metric of an experiment. A log is evidence that an analysis reads. This module computes no metric and gives no verdict.

kinds.detection-reviewed: An operator reviewed the signals and judged that the declared problem is present.
kinds.fault-injection-finished: The command that injects the fault returned. Record it after the command.
kinds.fault-injection-started: The control of the run is about to issue the command that injects the fault. Record it before the command.
kinds.manual-action: An operator acted on the environment by hand, outside the procedure of the run.
kinds.reversal-accepted: The commit that reverses the change was accepted into the branch that the delivery path follows.
kinds.reversal-created: The commit that reverses the change exists.
kinds.reversal-decided: An operator decided to reverse the change.

limitations: The instant recordedAt is the wall clock of the host that ran the record command, in UTC, to one millisecond. It is the instant at which the event was recorded. It is not the instant at which the event happened.
A wall clock can be set while a run is in progress. The end line names each event that was recorded at an earlier instant than the event before it.

A fault is injected between the event fault-injection-started and the event fault-injection-finished, when the control of the run recorded the first before the command and the second after it. Nothing checks that order, and no instant inside that interval is established.

The instant occurredAt is what the person or the program that recorded the event stated. It is on the clock that the event names, it keeps the resolution that it was stated with, and nothing compares it with that clock.
The difference between the clock of the recording host and any other clock is not measured.
An event of an operator is recorded when the operator runs the command. The time between a judgement and its record is not measured.
A code and a name are free within their form. The form is not a check for a secret, and it does not show that the frozen record of an experiment registers the code.
One process appends to a log. Two processes that append at one time are not ordered, and the tool does not lock the file.
A log holds at most 500 events.
omitted: The name, the account, and the address of a person. An actor is one of two roles.
Each note and each description. An event states a code and no sentence.
The command line of a fault and the text that a command printed.
Each request identifier and each correlation identifier of a caller.
The address of a repository and the name of a branch.
